thread.title: Profits are booming for Georgia's biggest companies (Slideshow)

author: Craig M. Douglas
title: Profits are booming for Georgia's biggest companies (Slideshow)
text: – Director, Editorial Research & Analysis, The Business Journals, May 29, 2018, 6:04pm EDT Corporate America's bottom line is booming on the back of a resurgent economy and the prospect that the good times are just getting started. As of May 23, some 3,193 publicly traded U.S. companies had closed the books on 2018's first fiscal quarter, reporting combined net income of $358.3 billion during the three-month span. The total marked a 26 percent year-over-year surge over the group's tally over the same quarter in 2017 and a whopping 63 percent increase over what was reported in 2016's corresponding period, according to a Business Journals analysis. More than half of those companies — 1,875 in total — reported a larger profit than what was recorded during 2017's first quarter, posting an average increase of 48 percent. Apple Inc . (Nasdaq: AAPL) topped all U.S. companies by generating $13.8 billion in net income during the three-month span that ended March 31, technically its second quarter of its fiscal year. The performance marked a 25 percent year-over-year increase for the Cupertino, Calif.-based company, which credited the banner quarter to a broadening of its revenue model in the U.S. and particularly strong iPhone sales abroad. In Georgia, companies had $11.12 billion in profit for the first quarter, up more than $7 million from the same period last year. Locally, companies based in the City of Atlanta earned $9.1 billion during that time, which is up from $5.65 billion in 2017. The Coca-Cola Co. (NYSE: KO) was among companies nationwide with the biggest net losses in revenue for the first quarter (down 16 percent) but was up 16 percent in net income. The Atlanta-based beverage giant also generally outperformed rival PepsiCo Inc. (Nasdaq: PEP), according to an analysis from Beverage Digest . Meanwhile, WestRock Co. (NYSE: WRK), which announced a year ago that it was moving its Atlanta offices from Norcross to NorthPark in Sandy Springs, saw massive gains -- with net income jumping 116 percent from 2017. The profitability spike among public companies has been attributed to several factors, although few appear to be as influential in boosting confidence among both business and consumers as the nation's resurgent stock and housing markets. Over the past 12 months, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has increased roughly 18 percent, while half of the 20 cities tracked in last month's S&P/Case-Shiller home index had reached all-time pricing highs. Other contributing factors include what many analysts have described as a looser regulatory climate for businesses as well as Washington's recently passed tax-reform bill . Much of the nation's newfound profitability has been concentrated within Silicon Valley. Google parent Alphabet Inc. (Nasdaq: GOOG) in Mountain View, Calif., reported a $9.4 billion profit in Q1, ranking it second behind Apple. San Jose-based Broadcom Inc. (Nasdaq: AVGO) ranked sixth nationally with a $6.2 billion net profit, while banking giant Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC) in San Francisco and Facebook Inc. (Nasdaq: FB) in Menlo Park ranked eighth and ninth nationally with income of $5.1 billion and $4.99 billion, respectively. The banking sector also had its share of winners in the quarter . JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM) ranked third among all U.S. companies with a net profit of $8.7 billion, up 35 percent year-over-year. Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) ranked fifth overall ($6.9 billion, up 30 percent), while Citigroup (NYSE: C) fell one spot outside of the top 10 with a total profit of $4.6 billion (up 13 percent). – Director, Editorial Research & Analysis, The Business Journals, May 29, 2018, 6:04pm EDT Related Content
